Now a potential hidden test: prefix "2001:db8::/56" with subnets includes values, but net.network_address for /56 has 4th hextet 0000? "2001:db8::/56" -> network address 2001:db8::. base + s<<64 yields 2001:db8:0:s::/64. Fine.

Now another hidden: /56 prefix where 4th hextet nonzero e.g. "2001:db8:1234:5600::/56" base 5600, + s<<64 -> 5600+s? Wait earlier we determined +s<<64 modifies h4 low byte: 0x5600 + s -> 0x5600+s for s<=255 gives 0x5600..0x56ff. So subnet 3 -> 0x5603. But spec says "prefix.network_address + (s << 64)". Wait 1<<64 adds to h4? h4 is bits64..79; but h4 = 0x5600 occupies bits64..79? h4 low byte bits64..71, high byte bits72..79. Adding 3 at bit64 gives +3 to h4 -> 0x5603. Yes. Good. So for s up to 255, 0x5600+s could carry into high byte at s>255? s max255 -> 0x56ff no carry. Good.

Now but what if base /56 had h4=0x56FF (host bits not zero) -> invalid prefix since /56 requires low byte zero. So h4 always multiple of 0x100; +s stays in low byte. Good.
